chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rifah said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and some of them asked him about jewelry (gold ornaments), is there zakat in it? He said: 'No, even if it reaches one hundred thousand.'

key_terms.الْحُلِيِّ: Jewelry (specifically gold ornaments worn by women)

ai.seo_question: Is there zakat on gold jewelry in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on *al-huliy* (gold jewelry), asserting that it is exempt from zakat regardless of its quantity or value, even if it reaches one hundred thousand. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between gold held as wealth (*mal*) and gold held for personal adornment (*huliy*), reflecting the principle that zakat applies to surplus wealth rather than items used for legitimate personal use.
